title: Where does the live map of the orchestrator and workers live?
context: The hub gets a live map: the orchestrator role as a particle core whose ring shows context used, workers as stations around it, pulses for messages, red when something needs you. Decision 12 gives the screen to threads and the conversation, with the board on request, so the map needs a place that does not crowd the chat.

options.name: Its own thread
options.summary: A Map item at the top of the thread list; opening it fills the middle with the map, and tapping a station jumps to that chat.
pros: Full size, room for many workers
No change to the chat layout
cons: Out of sight while you chat

options.name: Strip above the chat
options.summary: A short live band over every conversation.
cons: Takes height from the chat, most on a phone

options.name: Small map on top of the thread list
options.summary: A small map above the threads; tap it for a big version in the middle.
pros: Always there, chat keeps its height
cons: Small, crowds past about six workers

options.name: Always-on strip that zooms to the centre
options.summary: A live strip above the conversation is always visible; engaging it zooms the map into the centre of the screen as a full view, and it shrinks back into the strip when you pick a station or close it. On a phone the strip is a slim band that opens to full screen.
pros: Full size when engaged, the own-view strength
Zoom keeps your sense of place
cons: Strip still takes some height from the chat

recommendation: Always one glance away without shrinking the conversation; the big version on tap covers what A offers.
reason: I like the idea of it being visible at all times, and zooming into the center of the screen when engaged. The strip idea is nice for an always on spot that can be seen. It needs to look and behave futuristically, think JARVIS from Ironman.
